newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi papers assail U.S. for Kurdish peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi papers assail U.S. for Kurdish peace talks.

text.p: Iraqi media on Thursday assailed the United States for sponsoring peace talks in Turkey between rival Kurdish factions who have been fighting for control of northern Iraq.
"The peace imposed by America (in northern Iraq)...is fragile and shaky because it is implemented in order to achieve American interests," the official al-Iraq newspaper said.
Rival Iraqi Kurdish groups began U.S.-brokered peace talks in the Turkish capital on Wednesday after more than two months of factional fighting.
The fighting broke out when the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) called on Iraqi forces to help wrest the main regional city of Arbil from the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).
The fighting weakened U.S. influence in the north Iraq -- effectively out of Iraqi government control since the 1991 Gulf War -- forcing a pull-out of aid and other programmes there.
Al-Qadissiya newspaper lashed out at Ankara's meeting saying that it was being held to "achieve the wicked American goals in Iraq."

Mediators in Turkey say they are trying to strengthen the ceasefire before moving onto the key issues of control of the city of Arbil and the sharing of revenues from a KDP oil trade on the Turkish border.
